Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target scores, wanted trade discount, on-time target, the largest share for one vendor, the days that count as on time and the score weights.
Check Team and Vendors. They hold the people and the vendors on trade accounts that every other sheet looks up.
Fill Trade Accounts with the credit limit, discount tier, rep and any annual rebate agreement of each vendor. Used credit and headroom fill in from Vendor Payments.
Log each purchase order on Purchase Orders and each delivery on Delivery Performance. Delay days, the on-time flag and the days late fill in for you.
Record each deposit, balance or credit on Vendor Payments. The open balance, days late and the overdue state fill in for each vendor.
Keep Vendor Price Lists up to date with the list price, trade price and valid-until date. The discount share and the expiry check show what to renew.
Write each damaged, wrong or short delivery on Quality Issues. The damage rate on the Vendor Scorecard comes from this log.
Mark price and communication on Vendor Scorecard each quarter. Overall score and rank fill in, and Vendor Comparison shows the best value vendor in each category.
Record every trade job on Trade Jobs with its quote, actual cost and rework days. Contractors and Contractor Scorecard show the true cost and the score.
Use Contractor Availability, Contractor Quotes and Contractor Payments to plan the next job, compare quotes and pay on the due date.
Check Document Checks every month: insurance, licence and certificate dates with the days to expiry. Do not start a job on an expired document.
Log vendor visits on Vendor Visits, keep Preferred Vendors by room type and review Vendor Risks on their review dates.
Use the 14 calculators for scores, best value, discount needed, rebate tiers, quote comparison, true cost, payment priority, credit, lead time, concentration and booking.
Read the dashboard and charts every week: order value, scores, on-time rate, balances, trade spend, overruns, booked days and expiring documents.

One row per month: fee income, FF&E sales, trades re-billed and the costs behind them; the revenue, the margin before labour, the net result and the margin share fill in by themselves.
Project results with margin and margin per hour
One row per project: contract value, invoiced, product and trades cost and labour at hour cost; the margins, the margin per hour and the two target checks fill in by themselves.
Fee income by month and fee type
One row per month: the fee income of fixed-fee, hourly and percentage projects; the total and the share of each fee type fill in by themselves.
Cash flow by month with opening and closing balance
One row per month: the cash that came in from clients and went out to vendors, trades, payroll, overheads, the owner and the tax office; the net and the closing balance fill in by themselves.
Cash forecast for the next 13 weeks with safety level
One row per week from this Monday: the receipts expected from open invoices, the vendor, trade, payroll, overhead and tax payments due; the closing balance and the safety check fill in by themselves.
Studio expenses with month and budget check
One row per expense: date, category, amount and payee; the month and the check against the monthly budget of the category fill in by themselves.
Overhead budget by category against spending this year
One row per overhead category: the monthly budget you set; the spending this month and this year, the budget to date, the variance and the year forecast fill in by themselves.
Payroll by month and team member
One row per team member and month: gross pay, employer cost and the pay date; the total cost and the paid check fill in by themselves.
Owner draw by month with limit check
One row per month: the amount the owner draws and the pay date; the check against your draw limit and the year total fill in by themselves.
Drawn this year to this month
Business tax instalments with days to the due date
One row per business tax instalment: quarter, amount, due date, pay date and status; the days to the due date and the urgency fill in by themselves.
Marketing spend and results by month and source
One row per month and source: spend, enquiries, bookings and the contract value won; the cost per booking and the return on spend fill in by themselves.
Source value scoreboard by source and start year
One row per marketing source and project start year: projects, contract value, margin and spend; the average value, margin per project, cost per project and return fill in by themselves.
Client reviews with rating, source and recommendation
One row per review: date, project, client, rating, source and comment; the month, the top rating and the follow-up phone fill in by themselves.
Client value with margin, days late and rank
One row per client: projects, contract value, margin and the average days they pay late; the repeat flag, the payment flag, the average value and the rank by margin fill in by themselves.
Goals with target, actual, progress and a behind flag
One row per goal: the target, the actual, the unit and the due date; the progress, the share of the time used and the on-track check fill in by themselves.
Pricing review with price change and margin effect
One row per price or rate you review: the current price, the proposed price, the yearly effect on margin, the decision date and the status; the price change and its direction fill in by themselves.
Insurance and yearly renewals with days to renewal
One row per policy or yearly renewal: renewal date, amount, cover and a note for the insurer or provider; the days to renewal and the renewal check fill in by themselves.
One row per client with projects: the unpaid invoices by days past the due date; the total, the overdue part and the risk check fill in by themselves.
One row per vendor or trade account: the payments due by days past the due date, with the next 45 days counted as not yet due; the total, the overdue part and the risk check fill in by themselves.
Projects with type, status, fee type and value
One row per project, the same as in the other parts of the suite: dates, fee model and contract value; the amount still to invoice fills in by itself.

Fill Projects once; every other sheet looks up the project name, the client and the type from it. Keep the project ids the same in all your workbooks.

Record the cash on Cash Flow by Month, then keep 13-week Cash Forecast current every week: expected receipts, vendor and trade payments, payroll, owner draw, overheads and tax. A red row means cash falls below your safety level.
